subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Boeing 737 MAX Crisis
description: A quick, practical guide to The Boeing 737 MAX Crisis.

hook.text: Two Boeing 737 MAX crashes killed 346 people in five months. The cause was a software system pilots didn't know existed.

buildup.text: Boeing moved the MAX's larger engines forward, which changed the plane's handling. MCAS software compensated automatically.

discovery.text: MCAS relied on a single angle-of-attack sensor. When it failed, the system repeatedly pushed the nose down.

twist.text: Boeing didn't mention MCAS in pilot training manuals. Airlines didn't know it existed until after the first crash.

climax.text: The MAX was grounded worldwide for 20 months. Boeing paid $20 billion in costs and faced criminal fraud charges.

punchline.text: One sensor. No training. Two crashes. 346 lives.

quiz.question: What critical flaw did the MCAS system on the 737 MAX have?
options: It could only operate during takeoff, not during cruising altitude
It relied on a single sensor with no redundancy and wasn't disclosed to pilots
It was designed for larger aircraft and couldn't handle the MAX's weight
